# Proteomics Power Calculator

> Interactive, client-side power and sample-size calculator for proteome-wide
> association studies (PWAS). It reports statistical power, minimum detectable
> effect, and required sample size / events for a single protein–outcome
> association tested across many proteins, under multiple-testing correction.
> This is a methodological planning tool only — not medical, regulatory, or
> statistical-consulting advice, and not a substitute for a statistician.

## Scope and intended use

- Purpose: study planning with aggregate or synthetic assumptions.
- Do NOT enter PHI, patient identifiers, or restricted/proprietary cohort data;
  all computation happens in the browser, but the tool is a public demo (see
  COMPLIANCE.md and the in-app data guardrail).
- Outputs are large-sample approximations for planning, not guarantees.

## Regression models (effect measure)

- Cox proportional hazards — hazard ratio (HR), sized by number of events d.
- Linear regression — standardized beta (β), sized by sample size n.
- Logistic regression — odds ratio (OR), sized by n and outcome prevalence, or
  by case/control counts.
- Modified Poisson / log-binomial — relative risk (RR), sized by n and prevalence.
- GEE / mixed effects — standardized beta (β) with a design effect for clustering.

## Study designs

Cohort, cross-sectional, case-control, case-cohort, nested case-control
(availability depends on the model, per the app's options).

## Core assumptions and conventions

- The predictor (protein level) is standardized to mean 0, variance 1; effects
  are per 1 SD increase.
- Two-sided Wald large-sample test. Power = Φ(λ − z_{1−α/2}) + Φ(−λ − z_{1−α/2}),
  with λ = |effect on the log/linear scale| / σ.
- R²_x is the proportion of PREDICTOR (protein) variance explained by adjustment
  covariates; it inflates every standard error by 1/√(1 − R²_x).
- Modified-Poisson uses a deliberately CONSERVATIVE naive-Poisson SE
  √(1/(n·p·(1 − R²_x))); the robust/sandwich SE is smaller, so power is slightly
  under-stated (required N slightly over-stated) except as p → 0.
- Multiple testing: Benjamini–Hochberg FDR uses a conservative per-test
  α ≈ q/m planning bound (true BH power is typically higher); Bonferroni uses
  α = α/m exactly. m = number of proteins tested.

## Source of truth

- Canonical math: src/utils/statistics.ts
- Rendered formulas (KaTeX): src/constants/formulas.ts
- Method write-up and equation definitions: README.md ("Key Calculations")
- Primary references with DOIs: README.md and the in-app "Methodology &
  References" section. Core methods: Schoenfeld 1983 (Cox); Hsieh, Bloch &
  Larsen 1998 (linear/logistic); Hsieh & Lavori 2000 (covariate/R²ₓ
  adjustment); Zou 2004 (modified Poisson); Liang & Zeger 1986 (GEE);
  Benjamini & Hochberg 1995 (FDR). Design-specific references are listed
  in-app: Prentice 1986 and Self & Prentice 1988 (case-cohort),
  Dupont 1988 (matched/nested case-control).
